title: Hardwired LED Ceiling Light: Wiring a New Fixture with a Wall Switch
summary: This Old House's Ask This Old House episode demonstrates upgrading a ceiling lighting situation by replacing a cord-hung fixture with a hardwired LED fixture controlled from a wall switch. The crew identifies hazards of the old setup, plans a new ceiling box and a switch location, routes power from a convenient junction box to the wall switch, and then from the switch to the ceiling fixture. They pull wires with fish tape, splice neutrals, connect hot to the switch, and bond the ground, using Madison bars to secure boxes. The LED fixture is described as having a driver that converts house power to low voltage, producing bright light at a low 18-watt consumption, and weighs about two pounds. The result is a flush-mounted, switch-controlled ceiling light that eliminates the prior hanging hazard and makes the room feel larger.
